name: NSE-SIM
_notes: NSE's Capital Market runs on the NNF Trimmed Protocol, which is not FIX
in any encoding: a proprietary fixed-width big-endian format with its own
sign-on, no sequence numbers and no resend. See docs/specs/README.md.
There are two listeners. 'nnf.port' is the gateway, where members trade.
'gateway_router.port' is the separate port a member dials FIRST, to
collect the session key, cryptographic key, IV and additional key that
encrypt the gateway connection. Both are joined by the Box ID.
A connection is a BOX, and many users sign on over one box -- which is
unlike either other venue here, where a connection is a session. The
'sessions' command lists users, because that is what an order's owner
means; the 'boxes' command lists connections. Disconnecting a box signs
off every user on it, as the specification requires.
'gateway_router.dynamic_iv' is how the dynamic half of the IV is laid
out under the 'new' methodology -- the one value here that is NOT
big-endian, since it is the memory of a C struct rather than a wire
field. 'auto' (the default) settles it on whichever of 'little' and
'big' authenticates a box's first message and logs the answer; set it
to either name to pin it and refuse the other.
To reach this simulator from another machine, bind 'nnf.host' and
'gateway_router.host' to 0.0.0.0. The GR response's IPAddress is a
member's only statement of where the gateway is, so a gateway bound to
every interface answers with the address that member reached the router
on; 'gateway_router.advertise_host' (15 characters at most, the width
of the field) overrides that for a NAT or a port forward.
'gateway_router.encryption' picks the published methodology: 'existing'
is AES-256-GCM used as a keystream with an MD5 in the packet prefix, and
'new' is authenticated GCM whose tag displaces that MD5. A member is
entitled to one or the other by which router port it dials; this
simulator serves whichever is configured here.
'gateway_router.tls' accepts '1.3' (the default, and what the
specification requires), '1.2' (a development floor, not a ceiling --
under OpenSSL 3.x it still negotiates 1.3 when both ends can), or 'none'
for plain TCP. A real member's client pins both the minimum AND the
maximum proto version to TLS 1.3, so it offers only 1.3 and will not
negotiate down to a '1.2' router -- '1.2' exists only for an interpreter
that cannot do 1.3 at all, such as this project's own Windows dev box on
OpenSSL 1.0.2. On such an interpreter, '1.3' is refused at start-up
rather than silently served as something weaker; set 'tls' to '1.2' or
'none' there instead. The Gateway Router's self-signed CA lands at
'var/tls/gr_ca_cert1.pem' by default (override with 'tls_dir', or supply
an externally issued certificate via 'tls_cert'/'tls_key'/'tls_ca_cert'),
and that file is what a member's client must trust. Recorded in
rules.ASSUMPTIONS.
'require_encryption' true holds a member to the whole Chapter 10
sequence: a box that never collected a key from the router is refused at
registration. False, the default, lets a client be pointed straight at
the gateway while it is being brought up.
Box 3 carries no users and is never dialled at the gateway (port 9021) --
it exists only so scenarios/20-nse-gateway-router.json can collect real
secrets from the router without touching a box (1 or 2) that other NSE
scenarios also sign on to in the clear. A box that has collected secrets
encrypts every message after SECURE_BOX_REGISTRATION_REQUEST, on a
process-lifetime box id, not per connection -- reusing box 1 or 2 for a
successful GR_REQUEST would silently break any later cleartext scenario
that dials the same box id in the same daemon.
Only the Regular Lot book of the Normal market is traded. Special Terms,
Stop Loss, Odd Lot, Spot, Auction and Call Auction 2 are rejected with
ERR_INVALID_BOOK_TYPE, and All Or None, Minimum Fill, disclosed quantity
and GTC/GTD orders are rejected too -- see 'venue.assumptions'.
There is no self-trade prevention: NNF Capital Market has none, and the
core's per-market mode keys on the participant code, which means
something else here. A market configured with any stp_mode but NONE is
refused at start-up rather than silently honoured.
Reference data defaults to the CSVs in exchangesim/venues/nse/reference/.
Override with:
"reference": {
"securities": "reference/securities.csv",
"tick_sizes": "reference/tick_sizes.csv",
"price_bands": "reference/price_bands.csv"
Paths are resolved relative to this file. A security's daily price range
comes from the 'band' column of securities.csv, because NSE sets it per
scrip rather than by a published price ladder.
